item.content:encoded:
This is alright. The stuff with Petra was kind of interesting, and I would be interested to see if you go anywhere with it.

Overall, though, it's more of the same "elder critic scolds the younguns for being so foolish and nihilistic and generally awful hipsters" narrative that has become the default for anything relating to Are We Cool Yet?, as well as pretty much anything relating to art more generally (see also: Critiquing a Cardboard Box for the most recent example). It's a theme that has come up time and time again, and by this point is more than a little tiresome.

Honestly, if we're going to keep with this trend of AWCY-as-meta-commentary, I prefer that it go in a direction other than "newbies amirite?"

Despite some interesting touches and some good imagery, it's just too samey for my tastes. -1

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Can I add the Are We Cool Yet? tag? I'm assuming the loathed logo mentioned in the story is "Are We Cool Yet?"

This is much more refined than the draft I read (and didn't critique). It leaves a lot of questions, but it also tells us exactly what we need to know. It doesn't tell us what emotion to feel, but it does make the reader feel emotion. It does still have some aspect of its weird "this came in a dream" quality to it, which serves it well enough.

Overall, good job, sirpudding. If this is your first tale, it's definitely a good way to get started; it also feels like a meta story critiquing AWCY? as a GOI/in-universe movement, which seems to be in-vogue now, but this takes advantage of it without feeling like the whole point is "I made fun of AWCY?. Am I cool yet?" I feel like that is gonna become a trend pretty soon, but this is ahead of that curve and therefore doesn't feel, well, like it's trying to be cool. Because it isn't trying, it simply is. Eugh, I'm digressing. Here, this is an appropriately disturbing story, you've earned your upvote.
